title: Mocking of a function within an api call doesn't work in FastAPI
body:
### First Check

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
`conftest.py`

    @pytest.fixture(scope="function")
    def get_client():
        client = TestClient(app)
        yield client

`utils.py`

    def sample_function() -> str:
        return "Hello, World!"

`api.py`

    from src.utils import sample_function

    @router.get(
        "/test-api",
        status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
    )
    def sample_api() -> JSONResponse:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
            content=sample_function(),
        )

`tests.py`

    from src.api import sample_api

    @patch("src.path.to.api.sample_function")
    def test_sample_api(
        mock_sample_function,
        get_client,
    ):
    
        mock_sample_function.return_value = "Bye World!"
    
        response = get_client.get(
            "/test-api",
        )
        assert json.loads(response.body) == "Bye World!"
    
    @patch("src.path.to.api.sample_function")
    def test_sample_api_function(
        mock_sample_function,
    ):
    
        mock_sample_function.return_value = "Bye World!"
    
        response = sample_api()
        assert json.loads(response.body) == "Bye World!"
```


### Description

I'm trying to mock a function which is being called within an API call in a FastAPI project. But the mock doesn't work. I've prepared a sample API to demonstrate the issue.

`conftest.py`

    @pytest.fixture(scope="function")
    def get_client():
        client = TestClient(app)
        yield client

`utils.py`

    def sample_function() -> str:
        return "Hello, World!"

`api.py`

    from src.utils import sample_function

    @router.get(
        "/test-api",
        status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
    )
    def sample_api() -> JSONResponse:
        return JSONResponse(
            status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
            content=sample_function(),
        )

`tests.py`

    from src.api import sample_api

    @patch("src.path.to.api.sample_function")
    def test_sample_api(
        mock_sample_function,
        get_client,
    ):
    
        mock_sample_function.return_value = "Bye World!"
    
        response = get_client.get(
            "/test-api",
        )
        assert json.loads(response.body) == "Bye World!"
    
    @patch("src.path.to.api.sample_function")
    def test_sample_api_function(
        mock_sample_function,
    ):
    
        mock_sample_function.return_value = "Bye World!"
    
        response = sample_api()
        assert json.loads(response.body) == "Bye World!"


In this sample if I try `test_sample_api_function` mocking works well, but if I try the test which actually test the api call `test_sample_api`, it can't mock the `sample_function` method.

Why is this happening and what am I missing here?

### Operating System

macOS

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.115.12

### Pydantic Version

2.4.1

### Python Version

3.11

### Additional Context

_No response_
